Royaume de France (moderne).porteur: Kings of France, from the late 14th century

Couronne d'Aragon.porteur: Kings of Aragon and Counts of Barcelona

Ordre de Saint-Jean (Hospitaliers).porteur: Order of the Hospital; plain cross

Royaume de Valence.porteur: former kingdom of the Iberian Peninsula

Premier Empire.porteur: the first of the two French empires established for the Bonaparte dynasty, from 1804 to 1814

Empire britannique.porteur: the territories conquered, exploited and dominated by England and then the United Kingdom, from the early 17th to the late 20th century

Royaume de Gwynedd.porteur: kingdom of North Wales, from the 5th to the 13th century

Royaume de Grenade (couronne de Castille.porteur: vassal province of Castile from 1492 to 1833

Royaume des Pays-Bas.porteur: sovereign state and transcontinental constitutional monarchy

Province de Brandebourg.porteur: province of the Kingdom of Prussia (arms of 1880)

Royaume d'Irak.porteur: independent state of the Middle East, from 1932 to 1958

Royaume de Karthli.porteur: monarchy of the late Middle Ages and early modern period in eastern Georgia

Royaume de Saxe.porteur: former kingdom (1806-1918) — greater arms with quarters (Meissen, Thuringia, the two Palatinates, Vogtland and others), not blazoned here

Royaume du Hedjaz.porteur: Hussein bin Ali, King of Hejaz (1916-1924), who also proclaimed himself caliph in 1924

Maison d'Este.porteur: Lords of Ferrara, before the French grant of 1431

Comté de Toulouse.porteur: Counts of Toulouse (778-1271), then the province of Languedoc

Duché de Brabant.porteur: Dukes of Brabant; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Comté de Flandre.porteur: Counts of Flanders; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Comté de Hollande.porteur: Counts of Holland; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Comté de Zélande.porteur: Counts of Zeeland; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Duché de Gueldre.porteur: Dukes of Guelders, arms of the union with Jülich (1379-1423), kept afterwards; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Comté de Hainaut.porteur: Counts of Hainaut; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Comté d'Artois.porteur: Counts of Artois; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Comté de Namur.porteur: Counts of Namur; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Duché de Limbourg.porteur: Dukes of Limburg; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Seigneurie de Malines.porteur: Lords then Counts of Mechelen; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Principauté d'Utrecht.porteur: Prince-Bishops of Utrecht (the Sticht); one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Comté de Zutphen.porteur: Counts of Zutphen; one of the Seventeen Provinces united by Charles V (1549)

Maison d'Oldenbourg.porteur: house of the Kings of Denmark, of Norway, of Sweden (Holstein-Gottorp), of Greece

Maison de Wettin (Misnie).porteur: Margraves of Meissen, then Electors and Kings of Saxony, Dukes of Saxe-Coburg

Maison de Wittelsbach (Bavière).porteur: Dukes, Electors and Kings of Bavaria; Counts Palatine of the Rhine

Maison de Lorraine.porteur: Dukes of Lorraine; branches of Vaudémont, Guise and Flanders

Seigneurs de Lusignan.porteur: Lords of Lusignan (Poitou); the Kings of Cyprus added a lion

Duché de Normandie.porteur: Dukes of Normandy, then the province of Normandy

Comtat Venaissin.porteur: Comtat Venaissin, land of the popes

Maison de Durfort.porteur: House of Durfort (Dukes of Duras and Lorges)

Édouard III d'Angleterre.desc: By claiming the crown of France in 1340, Edward III quartered his arms with those of France — at first “ancient” France (semé of lilies).

Édouard de Woodstock, le Prince Noir.nom: Edward of Woodstock, the Black Prince
Édouard de Woodstock, le Prince Noir.desc: The silver label is the heir's mark of difference: these are his “arms of peace”, distinct from those of the king his father.

Bertrand du Guesclin.desc: Great captain of the Hundred Years' War; his arms appear in the Gelre Armorial. The bendlet is a mark of difference here.

Edmond FitzAlan (2e comte d'Arundel).desc: Arms of the FitzAlans, Earls of Arundel. The rolls of arms consulted record them for Richard FitzAlan (1300), not for him personally.

John FitzAlan.desc: Arms of the FitzAlans, Earls of Arundel. The rolls of arms consulted record them for Richard FitzAlan (1300), not for him personally.

Richard FitzAlan.desc: The Falkirk Roll, Glover's Roll and the poem of Caerlaverock (1300) give him these arms, which also appear on his seal on the Barons' Letter (1301). The FitzAlans had them from the d'Aubignys, Earls of Arundel before them.

Paul IV.meta: 1476–1559 · 223rd pope of the Catholic Church, from 1555 to 1559

Pie II.meta: 1405–1464 · 210th pope of the Catholic Church, from 1458 to 1464

Margrethe II.meta: b. 1940 · Queen of Denmark from 1972 to 2024
Margrethe II.desc: In 1972, the queen simplified the royal arms: she removed the quarters of the Wends and Goths, Holstein, Stormarn, Dithmarschen, Lauenburg and Delmenhorst, and straightened the arms of the cross.

Nanker.meta: 1270–1341 · Polish Catholic bishop, ordinary of Kraków and then of Wrocław

Famille Fleming.meta: Anna Fleming (1562–1608), Herman Fleming (1579–1652) and Claes Fleming (1617–1669)

Gregers Matsson.meta: d. 1494 · riksråd and lagman, in Sweden
Gregers Matsson.desc: The arms of the medieval family known as Lillie, taken up by his father Matts Ödgislason. Another Lillie family, introduced to the House of Nobility in 1625, claimed descent from it, which is now thought unlikely, and bore the reverse tinctures: or, a fleur-de-lis azure.

Jean-Baptiste Colbert.meta: 1619–1683 · Controller-General of Finances to Louis XIV
Jean-Baptiste Colbert.desc: Canting arms: the Latin for grass snake is coluber. Motto: “Pro rege saepe, pro patria semper” (for the king often, for the fatherland always).

Jules Mazarin.desc: The lictor's fasces, emblem of the Roman Senate, links the cardinal to the great figures of Antiquity.

Jacques Cœur.desc: Canting arms, taken on his ennoblement: the scallops for Saint James (Jacques), the hearts (cœurs) for the name. Motto: “A vaillans cuers riens impossible” (to valiant hearts, nothing is impossible).

Haakon VII.desc: A prince of the Glücksburg branch: once king, he kept only the lion of Norway holding the axe, with no more Dannebrog or Oldenburg.

Pierre III de Russie.meta: 1728–1762 · Duke of Holstein-Gottorp, Emperor of Russia
Pierre III de Russie.desc: Accolé: the eagle of Russia on one side, on the other the inheritance of Holstein-Gottorp (Norway, Holstein, Stormarn, Dithmarschen, Oldenburg, Delmenhorst).

Alexandre II de Russie.meta: 1818–1881 · Emperor of Russia, Grand Duke of Finland, King of Poland
Alexandre II de Russie.desc: His shield is now just the double-headed eagle with Saint George at its heart: the arms of Holstein-Gottorp have gone.

Constantin Nikolaïevitch de Russie.desc: An anchor and an arrow beneath a star: the admiral; his motto translates the Saxon “Treu und Glauben”, in tribute to his wife Alexandra of Saxe-Altenburg.

Michel Nikolaïevitch de Russie.desc: The Romanov griffin holds a round shield with the bend of Baden, a tribute to his wife Cecilie of Baden; two cannons behind the shield.

Maria Nikolaïevna de Russie.desc: Per pale: on the dexter Leuchtenberg-Eichstätt-Beauharnais, on the sinister the imperial eagle of Russia.

Adolphe-Frédéric de Suède.meta: 1710–1771 · Prince-Bishop of Lübeck, King of Sweden (1751–1771)
Adolphe-Frédéric de Suède.desc: The cross of Saint Eric between modern Sweden and ancient Sweden; the shield of Holstein-Gottorp over all.

Charles XIII de Suède et de Norvège.nom: Charles XIII of Sweden and Norway
Charles XIII de Suède et de Norvège.meta: 1748–1818 · King of Sweden, King of Norway (1814–1818)
Charles XIII de Suède et de Norvège.desc: A pall formy brings together modern Sweden, ancient Sweden and Norway, whose lion now holds a halberd.

Georges Ier de Grèce.desc: On the couped cross of Greece, the escutcheon of his House of Glücksburg.

Henri de Monpezat.desc: Denmark in quarters 1 and 4, Monpezat (a lion and three stars) in quarters 2 and 3: the shield of a queen's husband.

Georges de Danemark.meta: 1653–1708 · Duke of Cumberland, husband of Queen Anne
Georges de Danemark.desc: The arms of Denmark differenced by a label with ermine-spotted points; his marriage adds no English quarter.

Guillaume, duc de Gloucester.meta: 1689–1700 · son of George of Denmark and Anne
Guillaume, duc de Gloucester.desc: The only surviving child of the couple; the shield of the kingdom bears the Dannebrog on an escutcheon, and a label charged with the cross of Saint George.

Albert de Saxe-Cobourg et Gotha.desc: His wife's kingdom occupies quarters I and IV of his shield, the barruly of Saxony II and III, and a silver label shows he isn't the king.

Léopold Ier de Belgique.meta: 1790–1865 · King of the Belgians, elected in 1831
Léopold Ier de Belgique.desc: Before his arms settled, an early variant bore the British kingdom in quarters I and IV, and Brunswick, Lüneburg and the rearing horse over all.

Léopold II de Belgique.meta: 1835–1909 · King of the Belgians, sovereign of the Congo Free State
Léopold II de Belgique.desc: The lion of Belgium bears at its heart the barruly escutcheon of Saxony: the Prince of Saxe-Coburg becomes king of a new state.

Ferdinand de Bulgarie.meta: 1861–1918 · reigning prince (1887), then Tsar of the Bulgarians (1908)
Ferdinand de Bulgarie.desc: A crowned gold lion on gules, with nothing Saxon about it; Boris III and Simeon II would bear the same arms.

Othon de Grèce.meta: 1815–1867 · Prince of Bavaria, King of Greece
Othon de Grèce.desc: The silver couped cross of Greece, with the fusily of Bavaria over all.

Frédéric V du Palatinat.desc: A per pale of Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia, Luxembourg and Upper Lusatia: the shield of a one-winter reign, after which his title of elector passed to the Duke of Bavaria.

Charles VII de Bavière.desc: The imperial eagle on a quarterly of the fusily of Bavaria and the Palatine lion, with the elector's orb.

Louise de Lorraine.meta: 1553–1601 · Queen of France, wife of Henry III
Louise de Lorraine.desc: Dimidiated France and Lorraine: on the dexter the three lilies, on the sinister the eight Lorraine quarters.

René II de Lorraine.desc: A shield that combines, the source page says, the arms of both his parents: Lorraine, Hungary, Anjou-Sicily, Jerusalem, Anjou and Bar.

Jeanne d'Arc.desc: Arms granted in May 1429, after the siege of Orléans was lifted: the Maid's sword supports the king's crown, between two lilies of France.

William Shakespeare.desc: Arms granted in 1596 to his father John, a glover of Stratford, and taken up by the playwright: the spear puns on the name (shake-spear). Motto: “Non sans droict”. The crest is a silver falcon holding a gold spear.

Michel de Montaigne.desc: Montaigne blazons his own arms in the Essays (“Je porte d'azur semé de trèfles d'or, à une patte de lion de même, armée de gueules”) and wonders what privilege this figure has to remain in his house.

Thomas More.desc: A quarterly of two designs: in 1 and 4 a chevron engrailed between three moorcocks, in 2 and 3 a chevron charged with three bezants, between three unicorn heads. The crest, a Moor's bust, isn't shown on the image.

Blaise Pascal.desc: The paschal lamb is the charge of the family shield, according to Rietstap and Bouillet as cited by Wikipedia; the link with the name Pascal is obvious, but these sources don't state it.

Famille de Gaulle.meta: de Gaulle family · arms said to be borrowed
Famille de Gaulle.desc: Arms that Wikipedia calls “borrowed”, that is, taken from another family: tierced in fess, with three oak galls, a field of gules and three trefoils.

Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet.desc: The arms of the “Eagle of Meaux”, according to a register of the clergy of France from 1723.

Jean Racine.desc: The playwright's arms, according to d'Hozier.

Cardinal de Richelieu.meta: 1585–1642 · cardinal, chief minister of Louis XIII
Cardinal de Richelieu.desc: The arms of the du Plessis de Richelieu family, which the cardinal bore.

Vauban.desc: The arms of Sébastien Le Prestre de Vauban.

George Washington.meta: 1732–1799 · first President of the United States
George Washington.desc: The arms of the Washington family, of England.

Talleyrand.desc: The arms of Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord under the Restoration: those of his house.

Gilles de Rais (avant 1429).meta: c. 1405–1440 · Marshal of France, companion of Joan of Arc
Gilles de Rais (avant 1429).desc: His arms before 1429; he later augmented them with an orle of the fleurs-de-lis of France.

Anne de Bretagne, reine de France.nom: Anne of Brittany, Queen of France
Anne de Bretagne, reine de France.meta: 1477–1514 · Duchess of Brittany, Queen of France
Anne de Bretagne, reine de France.desc: As queen, she bore the arms of France impaling those of Brittany.

Francis Drake.desc: Blazon from the Commons page, in English (“Sable, a fess wavy argent between two mullets of the same”), translated into French here.

Jean VI d'Aumont.desc: The arms of Jean VI d'Aumont, Count of Châteauroux, known as the Franc Gaulois, who died at the siege of the Château de Comper. The image surrounds them with his coronet and collars.
